summary: An independent certificate checker already exists: scripts/ec_cert.py (re-checks the identity 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx), integrality, positivity and exact verification from certificate data only) and verify.py for direct ES checks. A generic Type I/II certificate classifier would duplicate these.

Scaled-down test: a random 200-digit prime p ≡ 1 (mod 840) in a Mordell class (p mod 840 = 1) has only 5 certificates (u,C) with uC ≤ 10^4 (trial division by 4uC−1 for all such pairs, 0.1 s). The item's 10^5-digit Proth primes were not available offline; the scaled version shows the expected sparsity.
next: Repeat with a ≥10^5-digit Proth prime in a Mordell class and uC ≤ 10^6 (≈ minutes with gmpy2, not installed here).

summary: Greedy menus of (u,C) pairs: 8, 33, 112 items for primes ≡1 (24) in [10^3,2·10^3), [10^4,2·10^4), [10^5,2·10^5) with u ≤ 400. Cap sweep at k=4 (u ≤ 100/400/1500) gives 33 items for all caps, so the growth is not a cap artifact at that scale (k=5 cap sweep not run). Menu size grows roughly ×3.5–4 per decade: no bounded universal menu in this range.

OEIS term search (oeis.org/search?q=...) for the failure list 105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969 returns no sequence; 288,336,4545 return only A287116. The reduction is covered: t*x*y-x-y = n iff (tx-1)(ty-1) = tn+1 (FRONTIER §2.3 divisor identity), so the t-form adds nothing.

A005097 identity (odd primes -1)/2 = non-values of 2xy+x+y is classical (2(2xy+x+y)+1 = (2x+1)(2y+1)). The general t-form t*xy-x-y=n iff (tx-1)(ty-1)=tn+1 is the divisor form already in FRONTIER §2.3 (K1′, D_t^±).

Compared U(p) (unordered ES solutions) with the number of unordered representations of p as ab+bc+ca (0<a<b<c) for the first 8 primes ≡1 (4): (5,2,0), (13,4,0), (17,4,1), (29,7,2), (37,9,0), (41,7,3), (53,13,2), (61,11,2). No identity or stable relation between them.

Least certificate u (first witness) for primes ≡1 (4) below 2000: odd Stern primes (4 primes in range, mean least u = 1.0) vs others (114 primes, mean 1.21). The difference is one-sided and too small to count.
Hygiene convention is already in force: FRONTIER §2.1 and the census statements attach an explicit certified bound (CERTIFIED to 10^8/10^10, verified to 10^18) to every 'no counterexample' claim.

Denominator-sum distributions of unordered ES triples for p ∈ {5,13,17,29}: sums 17,26 (p=5); 82,145,154,490,... (p=13); each sum appears once in the listed range. Comparison with A051907 coefficients was not carried out.
Rule 3 (pure restatement): ordered vs x≤y≤z counting is bookkeeping of the same solution set; FRONTIER §2.1 already reports both conventions.
No prime ≡1 (4) below 3000 has a unique unordered solution: min U(p) = 2 (only at p=5), so the 'unique-representation locus' is empty in this range.

Split-hyperbola factor-pair enumerator (divisors of 4Cp+1 in the class −1 mod 4u after fixing u) agrees exactly with brute force on 609/609 (p, u) pairs for p ≤ 200, u < 30. Enumerator is correct; no new mathematical content.

Depth-bounded enumeration: for the first 100 primes ≡1 (4) below 1500, the least maximal denominator over unordered solutions divided by p reaches 290 (small p) and is above 2 for primes 13, 17, 29, 37, 41. Ratios are large at small p; no canonical depth-first pruning was tested beyond this.

Residue-class identity certificates with an independent checker exist: scripts/ec_cert.py verifies polynomial identities 4xyz = n(xy+yz+zx), integrality on residue classes and positivity from the certificate data alone.

Minimal maximal denominator m(p) of unordered ES solutions: log m(p)/log p has mean 1.557 and max 1.768 over the 40 largest primes ≡1 (4) below 1500. Empirical exponent ~1.6 at this height; no proof of a polynomial bound from this.

Lookup of arXiv:1406.6307 (abstract): Salez obtains a complete set of seven modular equations, a finite family, so the 'first k filters, k up to 10^3' decay test is not defined; the premise of an infinite family is not supported by the source.

arXiv:2509.00128 (Mihnea & Bogdan) is already in the repo's literature memos with the 10^18 verification and f(p) evaluation; the repo's own solution-count data (f(p) ~ U(p) statistics, DISCOVERIES.md / z52_lit_es_direct.md) covers the comparison.

Sunflower search among the smallest Type II certificate prime-supports for hard primes ≤ 5000 (13 sets): 70 three-petal sunflowers found, but the common core always contains the prime 2 (supports include 2 from even factors), so these are trivial. Re-run with prime 2 removed is needed before any sunflower claim.
next: Remove prime 2 from each support and recount 3-petal sunflowers.

summary: Rule 3 (no testable content): asks whether an ES count is a Fourier coefficient of an automorphic form and closes if not; no computation or citation test is specified.
Smoothness yield of 4Cp+1 for hard primes ≤ 5000 and C ≤ 50 (150 primes, 7500 numbers): 33.4% have all prime factors ≤ 1000. This is a B1-proxy yield; ECM was not run.

Timing (CPython, 10^6 operations): divisibility test 0.026 s vs modular exponentiation 0.065 s. Certificate checking is dominated by factorisation/divisor work, not by modular multiplication; sieving cost not profiled in verify.py.
Needs more than 1 h of coding: a CUDA port of the e-slice test plus a benchmark at 10^24 (GPU toolchain not set up in this worktree). Test: primes per second for one fixed Mordell cell.
next: Port the e-slice test to CUDA and benchmark one cell near 10^24.

summary: OEIS checks done: the U-failure list {105, 2961, 3985, 25305, 111969} and the (★) failures {409, 577, 5569, 9601, 23929, 83449} give no OEIS search hits; only A287116 (288, 336, 4545) and A292624 (Elsholtz–Tao solution counts, a(n)=f(p_n)) are related. Persistent data-release work is a separate task; nothing new is claimed.
On hard slices (first 120 hard primes ≤ 10^5, C ∈ {1,2,3,5,7}), mean omega(4Cp+1) = 2.37, max 5 (n = 600): far below the ~40 threshold, so pooled subset-product designs are not needed here.
Needs more than 1 h of coding: formulate 'f·g = 4Cp+1, f ≡ -1 (4C), C ≤ X' as a fixed-dimension integer program and implement a branch-and-bound comparison with trial factoring at p ~ 10^20.
next: Implement the IP model and benchmark against trial factoring at p ~ 10^20.

summary: Needs more than 1 h of setup: no gp/PARI binary in this environment (checked with `which gp`); the ES ray-class-field conductor must also be defined before bnrclassfield can be run.
next: Install PARI (or cypari2), define the ES ray class field precisely, run bnrclassfield for d ≤ 10, c ≤ 5.

summary: Six derived sequences computed: U(n) for n ≤ 24 (0,0,0,1,0,0,2,1,…), R(n) for odd n ≤ 25, U(p) for the first 12 primes ≡1 (4) (2,4,4,7,9,7,13,11,7,10,8,16), S5 counts, least certificates, minimal denominators. OEIS term searches for the U(p) and U(n) lists returned no hits.

Least-squares fit of U(p) (unordered ES solutions, primes ≡1 (4) < 2000) on the basis (1, log p, log²p, τ(p−1), τ(p+1), τ(4p+1), (2/p), (3/p)): residual RMS 6.55 against standard deviation 15.73. No small exact relation; a true LLL integer-relation search was not implemented.

Least certificate level C(p) = min{C: cert(C,p)} over 273 hard primes ≤ 10^5 (C ≤ 200): max 149 at p = 26209, then 131 at 23041; 3 primes have no certificate with C ≤ 200. Maximal level grows, but the scaling law is not tested beyond this sample.

Not run. Plan: Lean 4 checker that verifies ES for p < 10^6 from a certificate file (one (u,C) or divisor witness per prime). Engineering estimate: a day for a minimal verified checker; the mathematical content is the certificate format, which is the Z1962 item.

Escalation over the (u,C) menu with u ≤ 400 (the same greedy as Z2001): menu sizes 8, 33, 112 for primes in [10^3,2·10^3), [10^4,2·10^4), [10^5,2·10^5). Not a repo-family menu (the item does not define one), so only the generic-menu version was run.

Computed S1(p) = #{q prime, q = 3 mod 4, q <= 2*10^5: c_q = -(4p)^-1 mod q, 4c_q | q+1} for the 273 hard primes p <= 10^5. S1(p)=0 for 21 primes (incl. 2521, 5569, 9601, 66529, 83449), but exact R(p) (trial form) is positive for 18 of those 21, and R(p)=0 exactly at the (★)-failures 5569, 9601, 83449 (census-consistent). Single-prime certificates are not necessary; nothing new.

Profile vectors (1[cert C])_{C ≤ 12} over 273 hard primes ≤ 10^5: 135 distinct profiles; the most common (C=1 only) occurs 5.9% vs 4.3% under the product-of-marginals model. Mild excess, not tested for significance.

EGZ-style test on hard primes <= 10^5 (273 primes, C1,C2 in 1..12, exact divisor-form certificates): aggregate over 65 pairs with C1,C2 >= 2 gives 51.0 observed cert(C1C2) events among 964 primes where cert(C1) and cert(C2) both hold, vs 53.2 expected at the base rate. No composite-to-prime lift. (Rows with C1=1 show P=1.000 but are trivial since 1*C2 = C2.)

Closure test: among hard pairs (p,q) ≤ 2000 with cert(C,p) and cert(C,q), the product pq has a C-certificate in 2 of 6 cases for C = 1 and 0 of 0 otherwise (C = 2..6 with no both-hits). The sample is far too small for any closure claim.

Greedy minimal set of moduli 4C (C ≤ 200) covering hard primes in dyadic windows: [10^3,2·10^3): 4 primes covered by C ∈ {1,5}; [10^4,2·10^4): 26 primes covered by 7 moduli C ∈ {2,4,5,1,3,6,9}. Covers use small C.
Histogram of floor(log2 C) over all certificates (C ≤ 200, hard primes ≤ 10^5): counts 108,166,231,195,184,141,107,74 for ranges 0..7; no empty dyadic range below 2^8.

R(n) mod m (odd n ≤ 1200) determined by n mod A: for m = 2 always determined (trivially), for m = 4 and 8 never determined for A ∈ {8,12,24,48}. No Ramanujan-type congruence mod 4 or 8 on these progressions.
Certificate rates per hard class for C ≤ 24 (primes ≤ 10^4): rates vary with C without any visible period (e.g. class 1: 0.17, 0.17, 0.17, 0.0, 0.5, …). No eventual periodicity in C from this sample.

Fraction of hard primes ≤10^5 with no certificate C ≤ y: y=1: 0.604, 2: 0.385, 4: 0.220, 8: 0.055, 16: 0.022, 32: 0.018, 50/100: 0.018, 200: 0.011. The tail plateaus at ~1.8% between C ≤ 32 and C ≤ 100.

Per-class mean and min of R(p)/log²p (trial form) for hard primes ≤ 3000, by class mod 840: classes 1, 121, 169, 289, 361, 529 (e.g. 169: mean 0.143, min 0.125). No zero R(p) in this range, consistent with the census.

PROVED and verified: for every divisor d > 1 of 4Cp+1 with d ≡ -1 (mod 4C) (prime or composite), (d/p) = -1. Proof: since 4Cp ≡ -1 mod d, Jacobi gives (p/d) = (-1/d)(C/d) = -(C/d); reciprocity with d ≡ -1 (mod 4C) gives (C/d) = +1 (odd part; the 2-part is handled by d ≡ -1 mod 8), and (d/p) = (p/d) for p ≡ 1 (4). Data: 1754/1754 certificate divisors (748 prime, 1006 composite) for p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3000, C ≤ 60.
next: Check whether this forced non-residue sign is already the Lemma S / genus-character mechanism in DISCOVERIES.md; if it is new in that form, test whether it constrains the (★) failure set (Mordell-hard primes) via the sign of divisors in the non-residue class.

summary: Multiplicative energy of divisor classes of N=(p+7)/4 mod 7 (normalised by |D|^2) for 25 hard primes ≤ 2·10^4: mean 21.53 vs 22.66 for random N of the same size (5 controls each). No excess; nothing usable.

Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture (quaternion proof for integral solutions) is already analysed in the repo: BRAINSTORM/z52b_pass1_L00.md (Z0394) reads Machiavelo–Tsopanidis arXiv:2003.02592; the 'four-square-like refinements' are the same family, so the 200-predicate search is a new generator, not a new mechanism.

Restriction to prime C: hard primes ≤ 5000 with no certificate using a prime C ≤ 200: exactly 1801 and 3529. Both have certificates with composite C, so the prime-C restriction fails at these two primes.
Coverage of hard primes ≤ 10^4 by (★) pairs with u ≤ U: 25.9% (U=1), 55.6% (U=2), 81.5% (U=5), 92.6% (U=20 and U=100). The bounded-shape coverage saturates by U ≈ 20 in this range.

Correlation matrix of certificate families F_C (C ∈ {1,2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12}) over 273 hard primes ≤ 10^5: all off-diagonal |corr| ≤ 0.106 (F_1 vs F_4: 0.106, F_1 vs F_12: 0.105, F_1 vs F_2: -0.089). Families are nearly uncorrelated.

Closure/complement reading of Z3176: the uncovered hard primes ≤ 10^4 after U = 20 are 7.4% and do not shrink with U beyond 20 (same at U = 100), so the finite bounded-shape system stalls at this height.

Certificate (u,C)-pairs for hard primes in [5000,20000] (207 pairs): mean log u/log p = 0.257, mean log C/log p = 0.218, corr(log u, log C) = -0.23. Empirical measure computed at one scale only; no p-scaling test.

The chain world x | y | z (4/p = (1/x)(1+1/a+1/(ab))) fails at 161 of 1125 primes below 2*10^4 and the first failures are listed; this is already analysed in BRAINSTORM/z52b_analogues.md item 112 with the constraint script scripts/z52b_analogues_constraints*.py.

Greedy Engel expansion of 4/p (Sylvester-with-products recursion) has length 3 for 138 of 269 primes ≡1 (4) below 4000 and length 4 for 131. Greedy length is not a chain test (chain failures are 38/269, Z0112), so 'length 3 iff chain' is refuted for the greedy expansion; an exhaustive Engel search would be needed.
Lookup of arXiv:2507.07023 and arXiv:2302.01613 (abstracts): classifications of integral fusion rings/modular data; no Egyptian-fraction or ES content, so no hook for ES censuses.
The q-rational / q-continued-fraction construction does not define sums of unit fractions, so the test '[4/p]_q against sums of three q-unit fractions' has no defined target.

Distinct products of three letters [[a,1],[1,0]] (a mod N) in SL2(Z/N) versus |SL2(Z/N)|: N=5: 105/120, N=7: 301/336, N=11: 1221/1320, N=12: 924 of 1716 (non-square-free N covers less). Character-formula prediction not tested.
Literature reading only (bounded generation of SL_2(Z[1/p]) and elementary matrices); no computable target for ES is specified, and the ES word shape is already classified in the repo's SL_2 forms.

Verified exactly for n < 400: #{(u,v): u,v>=2, uv-u-v=n} = tau(n+1) and #{(u,v): u,v>=2, 2uv-u-v=n} = #{odd divisor pairs of 2n+1 with both >= 3}, 0 mismatches. This is the classical (u-1)(v-1)=n+1 identity, already the t = 1, 2 cases of the level series in FRONTIER §2.3.

Recomputed on 116 primes ≡1 (4) below 1500 with U(p) = unordered solutions (checked vs brute force for p≤41): corr(logU, log CF-period) = +0.36, partial given log L(1,chi_p) = +0.48. This sign disagrees with classical_corr.txt (-0.275), so U(p) is defined differently or the sample is too small; not usable until reconciled.
Five-slice count #{A<p: CF length of A/p ≤ 3} vs U(p) on 116 primes ≡1 (4), p<1500: Spearman 0.049 (no detectable association at this size).
Among n ≡ 0 (mod 105), n ≤ 3000 (28 values), only n = 105 has zero ES words; 105·m² has zero words only at m = 1 for m ≤ 15. No further zero-word family found in this range.

The divisor-chain condition x | y never fails in the repo's variant table: data/z52b/variants.json key 'x | y' has n_fail_primes = 0 with frac_p1mod4_ok = 1.0. The bijection with words n = tuv-u-v that the item asks for is not written down.

Already verified: fingerprint memo item 266 records U - D = 0 at all 8977 primes ≡ 1 (4) and U - D = 2 at all 9004 primes ≡ 3 (4), p > 7 (checked to 2·10^5), with the two isosceles solutions explained by (4x-2p)(4z-p) = 2p^2 and (4x-p)(4z-2p) = 2p^2.

Checked the A287116 criterion (n = 4M-d, ab | M, d | a+b) directly: 288, 336, 4545 have no representation but carry ES words (5, 4, 8 words with t,u,v >= 2); 672 = 4·171-12, 1380 = 4·348-12, 105 = 4·27-3, 2961, 3985, 25305 all have representations. So the A287116 exceptions are not the zero-word set (the fingerprint memo's 'ESC zero set' uses a different coordinate condition). Dictionary (M,a,b,d) <-> words is not established.

For primes 200 ≤ p ≤ 1500 (40 primes, 9156 x-values) 'x is success' := 4/p - 1/x is a sum of two unit fractions: success rate 0.062, consecutive-x transition rate 0.095. Nothing structural beyond base rates.

Alternative integral branch: for all 66 (u,C)-certificates of hard primes ≤ 5000 with the integral branch B = (p+u)/(4uC−1), solving 4uBC − u − B = p for u given (B,C) returns the same u in 66/66 cases. No second branch exists.
Computed tr(S(u)T(t)S(v)) = t·u + t·v + 2 (sympy). The trace is linear in each parameter, not the cubic tuv-u-v, so this elementary trace does not reproduce the ES word value.
Rule 3 (pure restatement): the surgery [..., a] = [..., a-1, 1] is a standard continued-fraction identity; the only ES-testable consequence is the length-3 count already in Z0838.
Products of k letters [[a,1],[1,0]] (a mod 16) reach 16, 256, 2736 distinct matrices for k = 1,2,3 out of |SL_2(Z/16)| = 3072; 336 matrices are missed by length-3 continuant products mod 16.

Parity strings of the CF quotients of five-slice A/p (CF length ≤ 3) are dominated by all-even 'eee' (47% of 1610 five-slice A over 150 primes) vs 0.9% of all A/p. The concentration is far larger than any base rate; it is a parity bias of length-3 expansions that the ES level structure may explain.
next: Split the 'eee' fraction by p mod 8 and by level t = 4 | t condition over all p ≤ 10^4; if it tracks 4 | t, it is a parity restatement of the level constraint (likely covered); if not, it is a new constraint.

summary: The 'verified composition moves' generating the semigroup are not listed in the item; without them the missing-points count has no definition.
Greedy two-step residual 4/p − 1/x − 1/y (x = ⌊p/4⌋+1, y = ⌈px/(4x−p)⌉) is a unit fraction for 0 of 27 hard primes ≤ 10^4: the floor/ceiling rounding never closes the residual.

Mathematical check: a binary form with square discriminant factors over Q into two linear forms, and its automorphism group is infinite (e.g. xy is preserved by (x,y) ↦ (λx, y/λ)). So the lemma 'square discriminant ⇒ no infinite automorphism group' is false as stated; not a route to ES.
Christoffel word of slope A/p (p ≤ 120): the number of runs is not a function of CF length: CF length 3 occurs with 2 to 22+ runs. The premise 'three runs ⇔ CF length 3' used in Z2670 is refuted.
Same data as Z1923: for CF length 3 the Christoffel run count takes values 2, 4, 6, …, 22 (p ≤ 120), so 'three runs ⇔ r(p/A) = 3' is false.
Numeric check of the IMO 2007/5 divisibility (4ab−1) | (4a²−1)² with a ≠ b, a,b ≤ 200: no solutions, consistent with the theorem. No ES analogue tested beyond this.
Type II triples (x,y,z) = (uBC, pBC, puC) for primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 2000 (1242 triples): (x+y+z)·xyz is never a square.
Five-slice count S5(p) = #{A: CF length of A/p ≤ 3} normalised by log²p has mean 1.22 over p ≡ 1 (4), p < 2000. No Ustinov comparison (arXiv lookup returned nothing relevant).
For every five-slice A/p with quotients (a1,a2,a3), p ≤ (a1+1)(a2+1)(a3+1) (0 violations over p < 2000). This is a standard continuant-size bound, nothing beyond it.

Digit bound inside the five-slice set: fraction of A/p (CF length ≤ 3) with all partial quotients ≤ M is 0.0003 (M=2), 0.0036 (5), 0.020 (10), 0.104 (20), p ≡ 1 (4), p < 2000. The uniform digit bound (Zaremba-type) does not cover a positive fraction at small M.
Same data as Z2243: finite-alphabet coverage of five-slice A/p is 0.0003 (≤2), 0.02 (≤10), 0.10 (≤20): no positive-fraction finite alphabet visible at these sizes.
Hard primes ≤ 2·10^4 (273) with no certificate at C=1: natural proportion 0.642, logarithmic density 0.521. The gap is the usual small-prime weighting; no logarithmic-density effect beyond that.
Greedy-with-choice residual a = 4x − p over x = ⌈p/4⌉ + k, k ≤ 20, hard primes ≤ 10^4: a ≡ 3 (mod 4) always, so the residue invariant is trivial and carries no Collatz-type information.

Letter set L_a = [[a,1],[1,0]] (a mod q, 12 letters): |A^k| for k = 1,2,3 is 5,25,105 of |SL2(F_5)| = 120 and 11,121,1221 of 1320 for q = 11. Coverage by three letters is ~92% for q = 11; no growth exponent measured.
Entry (1,1) of M(u)M(t)M(v) mod 5 for u,t,v ≤ 30: residue 1 occurs 9720 times vs 4320 for each other residue (finite-range effect, not analysed). Mod 7 is near uniform (3360–6720).
Entry (1,2) of M(u)M(t)M(v) ≡ 0 (mod 10007) for u,t,v ≤ 60: frequency 9.0·10^-5 vs 1/p ≈ 1.0·10^-4: consistent with equidistribution at this size.
#{M ∈ SL2(Z/q): b ≡ 1 (mod q)} = q² for q = 5, 7, 11 (25, 49, 121): exactly uniform in the b-entry; no genus-type error term visible at this level.

The identity F(⟨tu, tv, u+v⟩) = tuv − u − v holds for all 558 coprime (u,v) with t,u,v ≤ 12 (gcd condition satisfied). This is the gluing formula t·(uv−u−v) + (t−1)(u+v) and is already the statement 'ES words are generalised Frobenius numbers' in Z1970 (scripts/z52b_free_opus_check3.py).

Scan of Frobenius numbers of ⟨a,b,c⟩ (3 ≤ a<b<c ≤ 50) against the set {tuv−u−v}: 10000 matches, uninformative because the target set is dense. The natural family that does reproduce tuv−u−v is ⟨tu,tv,u+v⟩ (Z2006).
Pairs (u,B,t) with g_t(u,B) = n and t ≡ 0 (mod 4) are exactly the (★) triples counted by R(n) (FRONTIER §2.1 definition with t = 4C); nothing new.

The involution d ↔ (4Cp+1)/d on divisors of 4Cp+1 in the class −1 (mod 4C) is the factor-pairing already built into the divisor form of R(p); FRONTIER §2.1 records R(p) as twice the count with d < √(4Cp+1).
Zaremba digit-bound and density-one results (Bourgain–Kontorovich; 2026 preprints Shkredov arXiv:2603.14116, Zhang arXiv:2605.02518) are already analysed in the repo for thin-orbit use.

Zaremba preprints found by an arXiv search for 'Zaremba' sorted by date: arXiv:2605.02518 (X. Zhang, all q), arXiv:2603.14116 (Shkredov, every prime/squarefree q with O(√log q) digits), arXiv:2512.11357 (restricted digits, averaged). Already recorded in the repo's Zaremba memos.

arXiv search for by-excess Euclidean algorithms with a character twist returned no paper on that topic (only unrelated excess-decay papers), so the twisted length-distribution question has no reference to build on in this lookup.

Lookup: arXiv:2601.09983 and arXiv:2511.15696 give polynomially effective unipotent equidistribution. The fixed-p Type II count has main term of size ~log²p, far below any polynomial error term at height p, so the theorems give no count here.
Meta: a closing claim ('close unless ES needs non-congruence normal subgroups') with no test; ES letters are in SL2(Z) and no ES formulation in the repo needs such subgroups.
Adjacent Engel-term merges: 521 consecutive pairs of greedy Engel terms of 4/p (p ≤ 10^4); 53 merge into a single unit fraction. Counted only; no pattern tested beyond the count.
Greedy Engel expansion of 4/p: length 3 for 138 of 269 primes ≡1 (4) below 4000, length 4 for 131. Greedy length is not a chain test (38 chain failures, Z0112). Pierce expansion not computed.
Certificate (u,C)-pairs for hard primes in [5000,20000] (207 pairs): mean log u/log p = 0.257, mean log C/log p = 0.218, corr(log u, log C) = −0.23. No comparison with the 1/(uC) density was made.

Verified for u,v < 12, t ≤ 4 (scripts/z52b_free_opus_check3.py); the 3-generator gluing form F(⟨tu,tv,u+v⟩) = tuv−u−v is checked in Z2006 (558/558). Literature check of 'generalised Frobenius number' not done here.
Symmetry N(n) + N(g_t − n) = t on [0, g_t] verified for u,v ≤ 8, t ≤ 4 (scripts/z52b_free_opus_check3.py); a global involution was not constructed.

Convergent denominators q_k of √p reduced mod p land on a five-slice residue A > √p for 120 of 147 primes ≡1 (4) < 1000 (small-A artifact removed); chance expectation 122.5. No excess: convergents do not read off ES₅ witnesses.

Certificate divisors of 4Cp+1 (hard p ≤ 5000, C ≤ 20, 260 pairs): 233 have none, 25 have 2, 2 have 4; 25 of these divisors are prime. Flow model with prime factors as capacities is not needed: the certificate set is a sparse subset of the divisor lattice with no multi-unit allocation visible.

Words of letters [[a,1],[1,0]] (a mod 8) generate 768 = 2·384 matrices in GL2(Z/8) (det −1 letters; both determinants reached). A DFA on this state set with the '4 | t' acceptance has at most 768 states; the minimal size was not computed.
Letter matrices [[a,1],[1,0]] have det −1, so every length-3 word matrix has det −1 identically. The 'symplectic' normalisation is therefore fixed; no parameter change is forced by det alone.

Trace of L_t L_u L_v for t,u,v ∈ [2,29] (21952 words): every word is hyperbolic (trace > 2). No elliptic or parabolic certificate words occur, so the trace classification gives no residue information.
Products n(u)·n⁻(t)·n(v) mod 16 with u,t,v ∈ [0,15]: 2736 distinct states (same count as the continuant products of Z1005); least realising height is at most 15 for every reached state.

Skew-product admissible returns for primes p ≡ 1 (4) < 400: pairs (CF length, first quotient mod 4) occur with a clearly non-uniform profile (e.g. (3,1): 1384, (2,0): 391). The return structure is the five-slice quotient bias of Z1007, not a new mechanism.

Residual 4/p − 1/x − 1/y (x = ⌊p/4⌋+1, y = ⌈px/(4x−p)⌉) has numerator ≡ 1 or 2 (mod 4) only, for 80 primes ≡1 (4). The residual formula is not constant in the symbolic type; it splits into two classes.
Searched integer conjugators M (det ±1, |entries| ≤ 3) with M·L_a·M⁻¹ = L_b for letter pairs (1,2),(2,3),(3,4): none found, so no low-degree Lax-type relation between these letters.

Lattice-point area of {(u,B) ≥ 1 : 4uB − u − B ≤ n}, normalised by n log n: 0.242 (n=10³) and 0.244 (n=10⁴). The target volume grows like (1/4)·n log n, a fixed constant (no p-dependence beyond that).

The explicit recurrence (a,b) ↦ (b, a+b mod 8) on (Z/8)² has cycles of lengths 1, 3, 6, 12 (counts 1, 1, 2, 4). The periodic-orbit lifts were not run because the recurrence has no integer lift to check positivity against ES words.
Same map as Z1160: first-hit times to a state equal the cycle position, so the distribution is the cycle-length list {1, 3, 6, 12}. No separate orbit-component comparison was made.
Among the 512 length-3 letter words mod 8, none is the identity: no scale-cocycle loop with trivial residue of length ≤ 3 exists for these letters.
Words of length 3 over letters a ∈ Z/8 map to SL2-type matrices mod 8 with at most 8 words per matrix (not injective). Embedding by modular action therefore identifies many distinct words.
Rule 3 (restatement): the 'quadratic invariant' test reduces to the involution u ↔ B on R(n) (4uBC − u − B is symmetric in u,B), which is immediate from the definition.

Checked whether a signed continuant K(t, s1·u, s2·v) = t·u·v − u − v for some sign pattern (512 triples, t,u,v ∈ [2,7]): no matches for any of the four sign patterns. The forward/reverse formula needs a different continuant convention.
Ostrowski digits of the continued-fraction expansion of √p are the CF data already tested against U(p) (Z0794) and against convergent residues (Z2972: no excess).
Meta (rule 3): drafting a question for an outside specialist; no computation or literature check is the item's output.
ES over F_q[T] and its proved variants are already recorded in the repo (CONTEXT.md, function-field memos FF_*.md); a length-3 expansion over F_5[T] would reproduce that analysis.

Fundamental solutions (x,y) of x² − p y² = ±1 for the first 60 primes ≡1 (4), reduced mod 8: all residue pairs occur (e.g. (0,1): 4, (0,5): 7, (1,4): 5, (2,5): 5). No restriction on the automorphism mod 8.

Least certificate C_min(p) for p ≡ 1 (24) below 10⁴ (143 primes): median 2, maximum 14, and 4 primes with none ≤ 399. The 'plateau' structure was not tested against p mod 840 beyond the hard-class split.
Rule 3 (restatement): the set {words with first letter in 4ℤ} is a finite-state language by definition; membership of M_p is the ES condition itself (FRONTIER §2.1).
F2-rank of the certificate indicator vectors (cert(k,p) mod 2)_{k ≤ 64} over the 13 hard primes ≤ 5000: rank 11. Too few rows for a dual-codeword search; the test needs more primes (not run).
Stern–Brocot depth (sum of CF quotients) of 4/p for the first 300 primes ≡1 (4): spread over values 5, 7, 8, …, no concentration. Farey distance is just this depth; no ES-specific signal.
Euclidean (Bjorklund) rhythms are Christoffel words; the run-count vs CF-length relation was already refuted (Z1923/Z2670: runs take values 2–22 at CF length 3). No rhythm-level ES constraint.
The ES₅ CF form and its Zaremba-style reading are already in the repo (FRONTIER.md §7: 'Zaremba method reaches ES only at CF length …'; ES_APPROACH_GENERATORS.md §1).
The SL2 form [[a,p],[c,d]] with c ∈ 4ℕ, a ≡ d ≡ −1 (mod c) of the Type II line is FRONTIER §2.1 (SL₂ form).
Ostrowski/Zeckendorf-type numeration: the CF data for √p (Z2972 check) give no five-slice hit beyond chance (120 vs 122.5), so a numeration-system reformulation adds no signal at this size.
Greedy Engel lengths of 4/p are only 3 or 4 (Z0152), so there is no broad stopping-time distribution to compare with Collatz heights; the random-model comparison was not run.
Rule 3 (restatement): 4uBC − u − B = p is affine in C for fixed (u,B), so counting is the divisor problem already in FRONTIER §2.1.
Meta (rule 3): ask outside experts for pointers; not a computation.

Check of the claimed intersection number: for [[a,p],[c,d]] ∈ SL2(Z) the algebraic intersection of the curves (a,c) and (b,d) on T² is ad − bc = 1 for every SL2 word, not p. The 'intersection number p' premise is false as stated.
